---
title: "17 — Sampling uncertainty for the composition-adjusted AI/AN gap"
output: html_notebook
---

**Research question:**
Does the 2025 AI/AN AUROC gap appear to persist once age-and-sex composition and approximate
sampling uncertainty are considered?

**Measures:**
paired original-versus-standardized AUROC gaps in 2025, using within-stratum PSU bootstrap resampling
with all model predictions held fixed. The resampling retains both populations in each replicate and
recomputes the standardization target.

This is a **sensitivity approximation**, not an official BRFSS replicate-weight
estimator or a definitive complex-survey confidence interval. It excludes model-fitting,
calibration, and harmonization uncertainty.

**Measures:** verifies that this notebook is operating under the current
numbered run and reading the frozen classifier.

```{r setup}
# Find the original RStudio project

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(current, parent)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

# Read the executable code blocks from existing shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(lines, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(lines) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Incomplete R code chunk in ", path)
        }
        paste(lines[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")
load_module("addon_insight_helpers")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
# Resolve the frozen model run separately from the current output run.
source_run_id <- get_source_run_id()
cat("[ADD-ON] New increment:", run_context$id, "| Original model run:", source_run_id, "\n")
```


## Reconstruct the 2025 survey sampling units

**Measures:** the source survey strata and PSUs, preserving the original
sample's clustering before restricting to the comparison groups.

```{r identify-design-units}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Survey clusters and fixed demographic support
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Map records to source strata and PSUs before restricting to the analysis groups.
# Keep common demographic cells fixed while replicate weights change.

# Build distinct design keys on all 2025 records before removing survey outcomes.
full <- data.table::as.data.table(load_source_rds("checkpoints", "07_scored_2025"))
if (anyNA(full$STATE) || anyNA(full$STRAT) || anyNA(full$PSU)) {
    stop("Missing 2025 survey-design keys; audit data before PSU resampling")
}
full[, stratum_key := paste(STATE, STRAT, sep = "::")]
full[, psu_key := paste(STATE, STRAT, PSU, sep = "::")]
psu_table <- unique(full[, .(stratum_key, psu_key)])
psu_table[, psu_index := seq_len(.N)]
strata_indices <- split(psu_table$psu_index, psu_table$stratum_key)

# A source PSU may have members from either or both population groups.
full[, psu_index := psu_table$psu_index[match(psu_key, psu_table$psu_key)]]
if (anyNA(full$psu_index)) {
    stop("Unable to map every 2025 respondent to a PSU")
}

primary <- data.table::copy(full)[
    cohort %in% primary_groups &
        valid_outcome(FMD) &
        valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT) &
        is.finite(selected_probability)
]
primary[, age_sex_cell := paste(AGE_BAND, SEX_CLEAN, sep = " | ")]

# Hold common demographic cells fixed across replicates; estimation weights vary.
common_cells <- find_common_cells(primary, "age_sex_cell", min_cell_n = 30L)
if (!length(common_cells)) {
    stop("No common age-by-sex support for the two groups")
}
source_model <- get_source_model()
selected <- source_model$selection

# Flag strata with one PSU; their variation cannot be estimated by this bootstrap.
single_psu_strata <- sum(lengths(strata_indices) == 1L)
cat("[DESIGN] Unique PSUs:", nrow(psu_table),
    "| Strata:", length(strata_indices),
    "| Single-PSU strata:", single_psu_strata, "\n")
```

## Recalculate performance under paired PSU draws

**Measures:** the unstandardized AUROC gap, the common-support standardized
gap, and their difference in each paired bootstrap replicate. The model is frozen; the
primary uncertainty is from resampling survey clusters.

```{r run-paired-bootstrap}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paired original and standardized gaps
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Apply the same PSU multiplicities to both groups in each replicate.
# Recompute standardized weights while keeping predictions and the common-cell set
# fixed.

# Return the two AUROC gaps for a supplied vector of survey-reweighted records.
calculate_gaps <- function(weights) {
    # Drop zero-weight PSU draws before calculating replicate metrics.
    nonzero <- which(valid_weight(weights))
    subset <- data.table::copy(primary[nonzero])
    subset[, replicate_weight := weights[nonzero]]

    original <- score_groups(
        subset,
        weight_column = "replicate_weight",
        scenario = "original",
        historical_prevalence = selected$training_prevalence
    )
    standardized <- standardize_weights(
        subset,
        raw_weights = subset$replicate_weight,
        cell_column = "age_sex_cell",
        common_cells = common_cells
    )
    adjusted <- score_groups(
        standardized,
        weight_column = "standardized_weight",
        scenario = "standardized",
        historical_prevalence = selected$training_prevalence
    )
    raw_gap <- gap_from_metrics(original, "auc")
    adjusted_gap <- gap_from_metrics(adjusted, "auc")
    c(
        original_gap = raw_gap,
        standardized_gap = adjusted_gap,
        change_after_restriction_and_standardization = adjusted_gap - raw_gap
    )
}

# Always show the exact observed point estimates before bootstrap uncertainty.
point_estimate <- calculate_gaps(primary$RAW_WEIGHT)
replicate_count <- if (run_mode == "quick") 99L else 399L

# Set the random seed before stochastic operations so the same inputs can reproduce this
# sampling sequence.
set.seed(seed + 1705L)
bootstrap_rows <- vector("list", replicate_count)


# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (iteration in seq_len(replicate_count)) {
    # Start all PSU multiplicities at zero before drawing within each stratum.
    counts <- integer(nrow(psu_table))
    for (psus in strata_indices) {
        if (length(psus) == 1L) {
            # Hold singleton strata fixed; this resampling cannot estimate their
            # variability.
            counts[psus] <- 1L
        } else {
            draws <- sample.int(length(psus), length(psus), replace = TRUE)
            counts[psus] <- tabulate(draws, nbins = length(psus))
        }
    }
    replicate_weights <- primary$RAW_WEIGHT * counts[primary$psu_index]
    result <- tryCatch(
        calculate_gaps(replicate_weights),
        error = function(error) {
            warning("Replicate ", iteration, ": ", conditionMessage(error))
            c(
                original_gap = NA_real_,
                standardized_gap = NA_real_,
                change_after_restriction_and_standardization = NA_real_
            )
        }
    )
    bootstrap_rows[[iteration]] <- data.frame(
        replicate = iteration,
        original_gap = result["original_gap"],
        standardized_gap = result["standardized_gap"],
        change_after_restriction_and_standardization = result["change_after_restriction_and_standardization"]
    )
    if (iteration %% 25L == 0L) {
        cat("[BOOTSTRAP] Completed", iteration, "paired resamples\n")
    }
}

replicates <- data.table::rbindlist(bootstrap_rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(replicates, "17_paired_psu_bootstrap_replicates")

# Percentile intervals are descriptive approximations, not official design CIs.
interval_rows <- lapply(names(point_estimate), function(metric) {
    valid <- replicates[[metric]][is.finite(replicates[[metric]])]
    if (length(valid) < 30L) {
        stop("Too few valid bootstrap replicates for ", metric)
    }
    # Use finite replicates for the approximate 95% percentile interval.
    interval <- stats::quantile(valid, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE)
    data.frame(
        metric = metric,
        original_point = unname(point_estimate[metric]),
        lower_approx = interval[1],
        upper_approx = interval[2],
        valid_replicates = length(valid),
        method = "fixed-model stratified-PSU bootstrap approximation"
    )
})
intervals <- data.table::rbindlist(interval_rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(intervals, "17_paired_gap_uncertainty")
print(intervals)
cat("[CAUTION] This is exploratory. An interval containing zero is inconclusive.\n")
```

## Show paired differences and their uncertainty

**Measures:** the distributions of the raw, demographic-standardized, and
change-in-gap estimates across the same bootstrap draws. The change reflects both
common-support exclusions and demographic reweighting. Zero marks no gap.

```{r plot-bootstrap-uncertainty}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paired-gap resampling distributions
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Display the original gap, standardized gap, and their paired difference.
# The difference combines common-support restriction and composition reweighting.

# Show the resampling distribution in the notebook and save it with the run ID.
long <- data.table::melt(
    replicates,
    id.vars = "replicate",
    measure.vars = c(
        "original_gap",
        "standardized_gap",
        "change_after_restriction_and_standardization"
    ),
    variable.name = "metric",
    value.name = "difference"
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
bootstrap_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    long[is.finite(difference)],
    ggplot2::aes(x = difference)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = atg_palette[["rose"]], color = "white") +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["burgundy"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Estimated sampling uncertainty of the 2025 performance gap",
        subtitle = "Identical fixed model; both populations share every PSU resample",
        x = "AI/AN-minus-comparison AUROC difference (or change)",
        y = "Number of replicates",
        caption = "Exploratory PSU-resampling approximation; model uncertainty is excluded."
    )
show_and_save(bootstrap_plot, "17_paired_gap_bootstrap", 10, 9)
```
